content: 1. The document titled NS in Pregnancy and Childbirth: A Guide for Midwives and Doctors was accessed on July 23, 2007, in PDF format. 2. Oral misoprostol is discussed as a method for labor induction, with information available on the WHO website, accessed on July 21, 2015. 3. The Clinical Practice Handbook for Safe Abortion was published by the World Health Organization in Geneva in 2014, with ISBN 978-92-4-154871-7. 4. A prospective study by Price ME, Fisher-Hoch SP, Craven RB, and McCormick JB in 1988 examined maternal and fetal outcomes in acute Lassa fever infection during pregnancy, published in BMJ (Volume 297, Pages 584–587). 5. Grolla A and colleagues described the use of a mobile laboratory unit for patient management and epidemiological surveillance during the 2005 Marburg outbreak in Angola, published in PLoS Neglected Tropical Diseases in 2011 (Volume 5, Issue 5, Article e1183). 6. Interim guidelines on the nutritional care of children and adults with Ebola virus disease in treatment centers were published by WHO, UNICEF, and the World Food Programme in 2014. 7. The United Nations Children’s Fund, WHO, and the IFE Core Group released guidance on infant feeding in the context of Ebola in August 2014, published by ENN in Oxford. 8. Updated guidance on infant feeding in the context of Ebola was published by UNICEF, WHO, and the CDC, accessed on July 22, 2015. 9. WHO published guidelines on the management of severe acute malnutrition in infants and children, accessible online. 10. Annex 3 of the Manual for the Care and Management of Patients in Ebola Care Units/Community Care Centres provides interim emergency guidance, published by WHO in January 2015. 11. A review of refeeding syndrome was published in the Journal of Parenteral and Enteral Nutrition (JPEN) in 1990 (Volume 14, Pages 90–97). 12. Kiguli S, Opoka R, Akech S, and colleagues published a study in 2011 on mortality after fluid bolus in African children with severe infection, in the New England Journal of Medicine (Volume 364, Pages 2483–2495). 13. Bausch DG and colleagues reviewed the literature and proposed guidelines for the use of oral ribavirin as post-exposure prophylaxis for Lassa fever, published in Clinical Infectious Diseases in 2010 (Volume 51, Pages 1435–1441). 14. The Sierra Leone Ministry of Health and Sanitation published standard operating procedures for observational interim care centers in 2014. 15. WHO published a document on psychological first aid during Ebola virus disease outbreaks in 2014, with ISBN 978-92-4-154884-7. 16. A guideline on palliative care, including symptom management and end-of-life care, was accessed on July 22, 2015. 17. The Advisory Committee on Dangerous Pathogens published a document on the management of Hazard Group 4 viral hemorrhagic fevers and similar high-consequence infectious diseases. 18. WHO and UNICEF published a document on key questions and answers concerning water, sanitation, and hygiene during the Ebola virus disease outbreak in 2014. 19. WHO and ILO published a document on occupational safety and health in the context of Ebola virus disease in 2014. 20. Favero MS contributed a chapter on naturally occurring microorganisms and their resistance to physical and chemical agents in the book Disinfection, Sterilization, and Antisepsis, edited by Rutala WA, published by the Association for Professionals in Infection Control and Epidemiology in 2004. 21. WHO published a rapid advice guideline on personal protective equipment in the context of filovirus disease outbreak response in 2014. 22. WHO published a guideline on hand hygiene in healthcare settings during filovirus disease outbreak response in 2014. 23. WHO published a document on key questions and answers concerning healthcare waste during the Ebola virus disease outbreak in 2014. 24. WHO published rapid guidance on the decommissioning of Ebola care facilities, accessed on July 22, 2015. 25. A preliminary report on health worker Ebola infections in Guinea, Liberia, and Sierra Leone was accessed on July 22, 2015. 26. WHO published a training package for Ebola pre-deployment, including a participant handbook, accessed on July 22, 2015. 27. A report on U.S. military personnel deployed in support of Ebola control efforts in Liberia from October 25, 2014, to February 27, 2015, was published in the MMWR Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report. 28. Dr. Jackson Amone presented a case management experience of Ebola at Kagadi Hospital during a stakeholders' meeting in Kampala, Uganda, on October 19, 2012. 29. Luigi X. Cubeddu published a review on iatrogenic QT abnormalities and fatal arrhythmias in Current Cardiology Review in 2009 (Volume 5, Pages 166–176). 30. WHO and UNICEF published an integrated course on infant and young child feeding counseling in 2006. 31. WHO published a training course on HIV and infant feeding counseling in 2000. 32. Support materials for a training course on the management of severe malnutrition were published, including participant resources. 33. The IMAI-IMCI Alliance coordinated the writing and editing of the referenced materials, with contributions from various experts and organizations, including WHO, UNICEF, and other international partners. 34. The original Uganda version of the VHF pocket guide was developed under the direction of Dr. Jacinto Amandua, with contributions from multiple experts and organizations. 35. The development of the generic VHF pocket guide and its adaptation for West Africa was supported by funding from the governments of the USA and Japan, with WHO oversight. 36. The IMAI-IMCI Alliance produced the final materials.
